doc.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Einstein and the arts and sciences
summary: She talks of Einstein, saying artists and scientists make human life possible.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: It's interesting that you mentioned him because I had, in one of the questions I had written for you, it was quoting something Einstein once said to his daughter, which was that if she was ever feeling really bad, to look to nature.
You see. Look to heaven for a sign. Yeah.
And he did play music, also.

I'm sure he did. People who practice the arts and the sciences, yeah, practice the sciences, it's the same energy. It makes it possible for us to live on this planet and not have fur all over and live in the ground. You can build your own house. You can make your own ambience. You can do anything you want to do. You can fly, if you know how. You can do anything you can imagine. So, we're not made imperfectly. We're perfect beings.
